scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-REQUESTER-AUTOFIX.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a response-handling/speed problem, so deploying an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix underlying billing errors will resolve it.

H-RULES-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused systematic bill errors (e.g., mis-handling of estimate substitution or read acceptance), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-DEGRADED.statement: AMI read delivery from the MDMS vendor degraded (missing/invalid reads via H-MDMS-BILL), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills since August.

H-FIELD-STAFFING.statement: Manual meter reading routes have been incomplete or understaffed since August (per H-FIELD-BILL), causing missed reads, estimate substitution, and billing errors.

H-TARIFF-CHANGE.statement: Bills are largely correct and the dispute increase reflects customer reaction to a legitimate usage or rate change rather than an operational data/process defect.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (2440 tickets) shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA — ticket response handling is already meeting its service target. This speaks only to response speed, not to whether underlying bills are correct or to the volume doubling itself.

Field route-log data (COMPLETE, AUTHORITATIVE) shows manual-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a material shortfall in field read collection during the exact window the dispute surge began.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate change was logged around the dispute surge window — the system of record shows no legitimate rate change event that could explain customers' bills changing.

billing-db shows 3025 disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED / 1785 ACTUAL; estimate substitution (the mechanism behind the AMI-degraded and field-staffing hypotheses) can account for at most the 41% tied to ESTIMATED reads, while the 59% majority of disputes were on bills already using ACTUAL reads, implying an additional error source beyond read-type substitution.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year; this is a stakeholder claim, not new tool evidence, and it agrees with the already-recorded AUTHORITATIVE billing-db finding (E-03) of zero tariff_change_log records in the surge window. It adds no new decision-relevant information beyond corroborating E-03.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortage of three meter readers since July causes routes to run late, resulting in estimated bills for affected customers; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder explanation offered for the route completion shortfall already seen in E-02, not new tool evidence, and SH-FIELD has a stated incentive bias toward attributing problems to staffing (seeking contract headcount increase).

crm-tickets monthly dispute counts show ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) rising to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026, confirming the magnitude of the surge the initial request described but saying nothing about its cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) establishes that the utility may request route priority changes but these are executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, grounding the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement in explicit contractual authority rather than mere policy assertion.

It confirms these estimate-substitution accounts are tied to manual-read routes (consistent with the field-read mechanism in the root problem) but contains no tariff, import-status, or validation-rule data, so it does not extend into the ACTUAL-read (59%) cohort cause the work item hoped to address.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) authoritatively identifies 14 specific manual-read routes with below-target completion values (e.g. R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity on the shortfall already quantified in aggregate by E-02. It contains only route/completion fields and no staffing, equipment, or scheduling data, so it pinpoints WHICH routes lag but says nothing about WHY they lag.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the 59% majority of disputed bills that were on ACTUAL reads (not estimate substitution) - a billing import validation rule change (H-RULES-CHANGE) or AMI data delivery degradation (H-AMI-DATA-DEGRADED)?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation scope should target billing-config rule changes, MDMS/vendor data quality, or both; leaving it open means the dominant disputed-bill cohort has no identified fix path.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Run query_billing_import_rules against billing-config to check for an Aug-2026 rule change, and obtain MDMS read-event data via request_mdms_vendor_access once vendor access is granted, then compare against the ACTUAL-read disputed cohort in DA-BILL.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the ACTUAL-read disputed cohort as an open diagnostic gap; do not claim remediation covers it until billing-config and MDMS evidence are reviewed.

U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the manual-read route completion shortfall actually caused by the reader staffing gap SH-FIELD describes, or by another operational factor (e.g. routing, equipment, scheduling)?

U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Run audit_route_completion_cause against route-log (DA-ROUTE) to examine route-level completion patterns and corroborate or refute SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-06) with authoritative data.
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Do not commit to a staffing-driven route fix; any push_route_update stays confined to the SH-FIELD-confirmed, contractually governed route-priority mechanism (K-DISPATCH) pending audit findings.

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Does dispute-volume returning to baseline actually indicate bills are correct, or could volume drop due to suppression/deflection (e.g. ticket auto-closure) while bills remain inaccurate?
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Determines whether dispute-volume-based success criteria are a trustworthy signal of bill correctness or could be gamed, affecting how success is validated.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Cross-check dispute-volume trend against independent correctness indicators (e.g., re-bill/adjustment rates, repeat-dispute rate) once analyze_disputed_bills_by_read_type confirms cohort causes, rather than relying on ticket volume alone.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report dispute-volume trend as a secondary indicator only; do not treat the volume-baseline criterion alone as proof bills are correct until corroborated by cohort-level root-cause findings.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07/F-05).
Of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,240 (41%) were on ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 (59%) were on ACTUAL reads (E-04/F-04), so the known estimate-substitution mechanism explains only part of the surge.
problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets at Lakeside Water Utility doubled from ~600/month to ~1,200-1,260/month between July and August-September 2026 (E-07) because manual meter-reading route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target over that window, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts (E-02); the resulting missed field reads trigger estimate substitution in the billing import step, and this substitution channel accounts for the 41% of disputed bills that were on ESTIMATED reads (E-04), producing inaccurate bills that drive a material share of the dispute surge. Response-handling speed is not the mechanism, since dispute response times remain within SLA throughout the surge (E-01).
